reason: E3 provides direct evidence that Si facilitates precipitation hardening via silicide compounds in RHEAs, supporting the first three premises. However, none of the cited evidence involves the specific TiVNbTa alloy system, so the claim that this alloy can form effective silicide precipitates without deleterious effects is unsupported. E1 and E2 are irrelevant to Si addition or precipitation strengthening.
premises: Silicon addition to RHEAs can form silicide precipitates
Silicide precipitates act as dislocation obstacles and provide precipitation strengthening
Precipitation strengthening can stabilize microstructure and inhibit thermal softening at high temperature
The TiVNbTa alloy can retain a BCC matrix with silicide dispersions
A modest Si addition will improve yield strength at 1273 K without unacceptable ductility loss
